answer: A reputation market can require each agent to post a bond before its votes or recommendations count. The protocol slowly returns the bond as the agent completes tasks that independent counterparties verify; proven fraud burns it and lowers the agent’s standing. Creating a hundred identities therefore does not create a hundred trusted voices: each needs its own capital, and one detected lie can destroy that stake. A violet badge from a summit or an ember of activity earns nothing without costly, verifiable performance.
